sentences.text: Author: Dipankar Datta Bench: Dipankar Datta  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL
APPELLATE

JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL No.5202/2025  [Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.16260/2025]
 SARITA PANDEY APPELLANT  VERSUS  STATE OF CHHATTISGARH RESPONDENT  ORDER 1.
Leave granted.
2. The High Court of Chhattisgarh at Bilaspur, by the impugned judgment and order dated 23rd April, 2025, has rejected the appellants prayer for bail in anticipation of arrest.

entities.text: High Court of Chhattisgarh at Bilaspur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. The appellant figures as an accused in FIR No.0411 of 2024 dated 31st July, 2024 registered at Police Station Bemetara, District Bemetara under Sections 34 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860.
4.
We have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties.
5. After the order dated 08th October, 2025 granting interim protection, the appellant has not been served with any notice to join investigation.

6. That apart, the appellant is a lady who is entitled to protection contemplated by Section 480,
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

7. In such view of the matter, we are of the considered opinion that custodial interrogation of the appellant is not required; thus, the appeal deserves acceptance and the appellant may be admitted to an order for release on bail in anticipation of arrest.
8. Accordingly, we set aside the impugned judgment and order.

10. Needless to observe, the appellant shall not, directly or indirectly, by making inducement, threat or promise, dissuade any person acquainted with the facts of the case from disclosing such facts to any police officer or to the court.
11. We clarify that the observations made in this order and grant of bail to the appellant in anticipation of arrest will not be treated as findings on the merits of the case.
12. The appeal is, accordingly, allowed on the aforesaid terms.
